name: 320 E Hastings St as built (public record): 11 storeys, four floors of First United community services, seven floors with 103 homes operated by Lu'ma Native Housing Society; the publicly announced money entered
proponent: First United Church Community Ministry Society (land owner, community floors) with Lu'ma Native Housing Society (housing operator)
rezoning_path: none: development permit DP-2020-00721 under DEOD Sub-area 1 (Development Permit Board, 25 Jan 2021; permit issued 15 Mar 2022)
notes: Same building. No program targeted (none of the real ones is in the tool). Money, all PUBLIC RECORD (https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2023HOUS0151-001731): other grants $40.28M = BC Housing $28.4M (Indigenous Housing Fund $15.3M + Supportive Housing Fund $13.06M) + CMHC $5.15M + City $6.73M (CHIP $4.83M and waivers); equity $34.0M = First United $24.4M (land costs and equity raised) + $9.6M still to be raised in Nov 2023. MY ASSUMPTION: land cost entered as 0 because the release folds the land into First United's $24.4M without a split, so the equity figure overstates cash by the land's value. PUBLIC RECORD: 11 storeys, 103 homes = 35 supportive + 68 rental prioritized for Indigenous people, floors 1-4 First United, operator Lu'ma (https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2023HOUS0151-001731); about 40,000 sq ft = 3,716 m2 of community space, 14 homes under $500 a month and the rest rent geared to income (https://broadview.org/?p=62916); all studios and one-bedrooms, 12 underground stalls (https://www.urbanyvr.com/?p=16166, 2020, which says 105 homes). MY ASSUMPTIONS: residential floor area 5,764 m2 (103 homes at about 40 m2 net over 0.72), hence total 9,480 m2; height 37.0 m; the 52/51 studio/one-bedroom split ('roughly even'); share below HILs 1.0; zero setbacks (a street-wall building); floor to floor is height over storeys. The floor area, FSR and height are in the Development Permit Board report (https://vancouver.ca/files/cov/320-ehastings.pdf), which refuses automated fetches and was not read. NOT PUBLIC, left blank: owner at completion, housing agreement term, accessible units. The programs targeted are the two the tool has; the real ones were BC Housing's Indigenous Housing Fund and Supportive Housing Fund, CMHC's National Housing Co-Investment Fund and the City's CHIP.

sources.title: Province of BC news release, 6 Nov 2023
